match.detail: no rule of the class wins a declaration on an element of any captured cell

entries.reason: Each class that styles nothing in any cell, or whose rules matched and lost, found by the browser instead of listed by hand.

CSS clips nothing here (`overflow` is `visible` initially, CSS Overflow 3 §3) and the set's root casts no shadow in any cell, so the capture-backed root leaves its layers unclipped, and a ring at its edge shows as in the browser. A root that casts a shadow still clips, since Figma draws a spread only from a clipping frame (PR2).

match.detail: a visually hidden child of the Field, which no cell holds

entries.reason: A row the recipe definition's hand-written omission explained, which a manifest may not hold. The capture reads what each element does in the browser: a class that won nothing drops once, and a class whose state no cell shows stays unmapped.
The recipe definition dropped the Field root's child rule by hand. In the browser it sets the title's width, as the row below reads it.
In the browser the Field root's child rule sets its child's width; the recipe build dropped it by hand.

In the browser the Field root's `[&>:where(…)]:w-full` (0,1,0) beats the title's `w-fit` (0,1,0) by source order, so the title is 100% wide; the recipe cascade gave `w-fit` the win. The title sits alone in its set, so it hugs its text either way.
